allFindings.detail: नहीं is placed inside the verb chain (बंद नहीं करना चाहता) rather than the more natural final-scope position (बात करना बंद करना नहीं चाहता = 'I don't want to stop'). As written, नहीं most naturally scopes over करना चाहता and the reading 'I don't want to stop talking' still comes through, so it is acceptable per negation-nahin-vs-mat (correctly uses नहीं, no मत), but the negator position is slightly marked. The decomposed lego मैं नहीं चाहता 'I don't want' does not surface contiguously in the headline sentence. Low severity.

allFindings.known: क्या आप आसानी से याद कर पाऊँगे?
allFindings.en: will you be able to remember easily?
allFindings.detail: Verb-agreement error. The future suffix -ऊँगा/-ऊँगे is exclusively 1st person (मैं याद कर पाऊँगा). For the honorific 2nd-person subject आप the correct future is -एँगे, so this must be 'क्या आप आसानी से याद कर पाएँगे?'. 'पाऊँगे' is a malformed form (1sg stem -ऊँ + plural -गे) and is ungrammatical with आप. The paana-potential construction in the contract lists पाऊँगा/पाएगा/पाया/पाऊँ as licensed forms; the आप-agreeing future पाएँगे is the intended one here, not पाऊँगे. Learner-facing USE example, so worth fixing.

allFindings.en: as soon as you can / as soon as I can
allFindings.detail: Known-side gloss inconsistency / soft ZUT issue. The lego जितनी जल्दी हो सके was introduced at seed 28 as 'as soon as you can'; seed 29 reuses the identical Hindi unit but re-glosses it 'as soon as I can' (the applied note acknowledges this, fixing person off the मैं subject). Same known prompt → two English targets cuts against the contract's consistency principle (aspect-to-english-tense: 'the same Hindi shape is not glossed inconsistently'). Defensible because हो सके is a person-neutral subjunctive disambiguated by the matrix subject (parallel to the vah he/she pattern), hence low severity — but the introduced gloss and the reuse gloss diverge and should be reconciled (e.g. a person-agnostic 'as soon as one can' or holding the seed-28 'you' gloss).

allFindings.known: मैं किसी और के साथ मिलना चाहता हूँ जो अंग्रेज़ी बोलते हैं।
allFindings.en: I want to meet someone else who speaks English
allFindings.detail: Two stacked naturalness wobbles, neither outright broken. (1) मिलना idiomatically governs से (किसी और से मिलना 'meet someone'), so 'किसी और के साथ मिलना' is slightly unidiomatic — के साथ here reads more like 'meet together with' than 'meet someone'. (2) The relative जो अंग्रेज़ी बोलते हैं carries plural/honorific agreement (बोलते हैं) over a singular indefinite antecedent किसी और glossed 'someone... speaks' (singular). Both are composed from legally-introduced legos (किसी और के साथ seed 5, मिलना seed 18, बोलते हैं seed 13) and किसी is NPI-licensed here under the desiderative चाहना scope, so no vocab/NPI flag — just a low collocation/agreement note. Related: the build fragment 'उन लोगों जो अंग्रेज़ी बोलते हैं' glossed nominative 'people who speak English' uses the oblique उन लोगों (correct only as मिलना's object), a minor case mismatch when shown standalone.

allFindings.known: मैं अभी अच्छा महसूस कर रहा हूँ।
allFindings.en: I feel good at the moment.
allFindings.detail: अच्छा 'good' used as a bare predicative adjective is a new content item. Only 'बहुत अच्छी' = 'very well' (adverbial) was introduced at seed 13; bare predicative अच्छा 'good' is a distinct lexical sense, not merely a gender-agreement variant of the introduced adverbial phrase. Borderline — flagging low because अच्छा/अच्छी share a lemma, but the 'good' predicate sense is unintroduced.

allFindings.known: आप अभी कैसा महसूस कर रहे हैं?
allFindings.en: How do you feel at the moment?
allFindings.detail: अभी was introduced as 'now' (seed 1) but is consistently re-glossed 'at the moment' here (main line + BUILD 'अभी कैसा महसूस कर रहे हैं' + USE phrases). Same Hindi token mapping to a different English gloss is a ZUT/one-token-one-gloss drift. 'at the moment' is a defensible synonym of 'now' so severity is low, but the introduced gloss 'now' should be kept for consistency.

Component decomposition glosses थे as 'you (past)'. थे is the masculine-plural/honorific past copula-auxiliary ('were'), a free-class item; it does not carry the 'you' meaning — that comes from आप + honorific agreement. The build/use glosses are correct; only the component-level micro-gloss is inaccurate.

थकान is a deverbal NOUN ('tiredness/fatigue') that is not in the introduced inventory. The only 'tired' the learner has been given is थका हुआ हूँ (s39, 'I'm tired'), where थका is a perfective participle/adjective from √थक — a distinct lexical item from the noun थकान. Lemma-aware matching: थकान ≠ थका. The controlled rendering of this seed's 'tired' should reuse the introduced participle (e.g. थका हुआ महसूस होने लगा है, masc., agreeing with the male speaker). As written it both introduces unintroduced vocab and forces feminine agreement (लगी) keyed to थकान — the applied note relies on that feminine noun to justify the form, compounding the issue. Affects the seed sentence and the two build/use phrases built on थकान महसूस होने लगी है.

allFindings.known: क्या आप सब कुछ समझते हैं?
allFindings.detail: This USE phrase uses समझना (समझते 'know/understand'), but समझना does not debut until s49 — its own applied note states 'समझना ... debuting here' at s49. At s45 the lemma समझना is not yet introduced (s8's समझाना 'to explain' is the distinct causative, not समझना). So this is a content morpheme used before introduction. A controlled USE here should use an already-introduced verb for the embedded predicate (e.g. याद कर सकता हूँ s10, जानना s17). The 'know'→समझना gloss also slightly strains, but the load-bearing problem is the premature lemma.

Component glosses are clean or use the explicit split-placeholder convention (e.g. मुझे...है = 'I ... is') for dative-experiencer frames.

family_scores.old_problem: s21 'उसकी नाम' = 'her name' was ungrammatical (नाम is masculine, possessive must be उसका regardless of possessor's gender); s24 old build had no person-agreement variance.
family_scores.new_handling: s21 fixed to उसका नाम with the English gloss carrying possessor-gender ('her name') per uska-uski-possessed-agreement; s24 fixed the future agreement पाऊँगे->पाएँगे for आप (2nd-person honorific) vs पाऊँगा for 1sg; s41 fixed लगी->लगा for masc participle थका हुआ; s31 fixed थे micro-gloss to 'were'. Agreement is now handled correctly and the gender-form variation is used deliberately for frame diversity.

family_scores.old_problem: No अपना appears in either build; the reflexive-possessive was simply not used (possessives are मेरा/आपके/उसका/मेरी, all non-reflexive in 2nd/3rd-person object position, which is correct).

family_scores.family: dative-experiencer construction (I like / I need / I think / I care - must be मुझे...है, not nominative मैं)
family_scores.old_problem: Old build had the predicates but with split/garbled components ('मुझे है'='I ... is', 'लगता है'='think is') and inconsistent framing.
family_scores.new_handling: Consistently and correctly rendered as ko-dative-experiencer: मुझे पसंद है (s26), मुझे ज़रूरत है (s44), मुझे लगता है (s47), मुझे परवाह नहीं है (s48), मुझे...महसूस होने लगा (s41) all use dative मुझे not nominative मैं, and the negated/question/2nd-person variants (आपको लगता है, आपको परवाह है) keep the dative. The cognition लगना (s47 'think') is correctly distinguished from the inchoative लगना (s41/42 'starting to') and the experiencer लगना (s26 'feel-as-if').

family_scores.family: positive-copula-negated / NPI in positive declarative (कुछ भी 'anything' used where positive कुछ 'something' is required)
family_scores.old_problem: Pervasive in old build: कुछ भी = 'something' used in plain positive declaratives everywhere (s4 'कुछ भी कहना'='to say something', s7 'कुछ भी कहना'). The NPI free-choice form was used as the default existential — a hard npiLicensing violation.
family_scores.new_handling: Fully corrected. Positive existential is now कुछ (s4 'अंग्रेज़ी में कुछ कहना', s30/s32 कुछ 'something'); सब कुछ (s45 'everything') in plain assertion; कुछ भी ('anything') is restricted to negated/desiderative/question scope (s35 'कुछ भी पढ़ना नहीं चाहती'). किसी (NPI oblique) is licensed under irrealis/desiderative scope (s5, s22). The applied-notes explicitly cite npiLicensing for each choice. This is the cleanest single improvement.

diff.frame_diversity: Strong and a major upgrade over the old build, which drilled new legos almost exclusively in the 'मैं ... चाहता हूँ' want-frame with mechanical recombination (the same few frames repeated with combinatorial vocabulary swaps, producing dozens of near-identical and often ungrammatical USE phrases per seed). The NEW content deliberately spreads each debut across contrasting frames: tense/aspect (s7 कोशिश करना dictionary vs s2 कोशिश कर रहा हूँ progressive; s9 बोलता हूँ habitual vs s1 infinitive vs s2 progressive — three aspects of one verb), person/agreement (want shown across मैं/वह-masc/वह-fem/हम/आप and present/past चाहता था/चाहते थे), polarity (positive vs negated dative-experiencers at s26/s27, s44/s45), and clause type (statement vs क्या-question vs embedded wh). USE-phrase counts per seed are now sane (~4) rather than the old 15-25 padded recombinations. P7-style frame diversity is genuinely realized, not just asserted.
diff.zut: ZUT discipline is the headline win. In-seed (hard) ZUT is clean across all 50: no case found where one known string maps to two target forms within a seed, and the want-paradigm is correctly handled as one English 'want' realized through agreement (a ZUT-legal one-known->one-target-lemma relationship, with surface gender chosen by grammatical agreement, not by a second English meaning). The understand-family trap is correctly defused (समझना/समझाना partitioned). The only residual is SOFT (cross-seed) ZUT: जितनी जल्दी हो सके renders 'as soon as you can' (s28) vs 'as soon as possible' (s29), which the loop's own s29 note admits should have been aligned and was not back-propagated to s28. ऐसा and कुछ carry slightly different micro-glosses across seeds but are bundled inside distinct whole M-LEGOs, so they do not surface as learner-facing collisions. Net: hard ZUT closed; one self-acknowledged soft-ZUT loose end.

examples.new: अंग्रेज़ी में कुछ कहना || to say something in English (positive existential कुछ)

diff.verdict: The loop closed on every serious defect family. The OLD build was, frankly, broken as a Hindi controlled-language product: pervasively English-calqued (verb-final word order violated almost everywhere — चाहता हूँ/legos placed in English SVO position), NPI कुछ भी used as the default positive existential 'something' (a hard licensing violation repeated across many seeds), a real gender-agreement error (उसकी नाम), and dozens of word-salad component glosses and padded 15-25-phrase recombination baskets. The FINAL NEW content is a categorical improvement: head-final and idiomatic throughout, hard ZUT clean, NPI/positive-existential correctly partitioned (कुछ vs कुछ भी, किसी licensed under irrealis), dative-experiencer frames correct (मुझे...है for like/need/think/care), agreement repairs verified (पाएँगे vs पाऊँगा, उसका नाम, masc लगा), the understand-family partitioned (समझना vs समझाना), and frame diversity genuinely realized across tense/person/polarity/clause-type with sane phrase counts. Two real residuals remain, both minor: (1) seed-47 uses यह before its seed-49 debut — a not-yet-introduced controlled-language slip and the exact class of bug the loop fixed elsewhere (s45), so it should be patched; (2) the seed-28/29 soft-ZUT on जितनी जल्दी हो सके ('as soon as you can' vs 'as soon as possible'), which the loop's own note admits was not back-propagated to s28. Both are one-line fixes. I would not mark it release_ready until those two are reconciled, but the build is fundamentally sound and a world apart from the pre-gate version — fix the two residuals and ship.
